keyVerseText: And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
rootMeaning: The root of מַעֲשַׂי (Maʻăsay) is עָשָׂה (ʻâsâh), which fundamentally means 'to do' or 'to make.' This root conveys the idea of accomplishing or bringing about something through deliberate action. The etymology as 'operative' highlights that the word carries a sense of active doing or working, which goes beyond a passive label to imply purposeful engagement in tasks or duties.
usageInScripture: The word מַעֲשַׂי appears as a proper name with a single recorded occurrence, translated as 'and Maasiai' in 1 Chronicles 9:12. It identifies a priestly figure descended from a notable lineage, emphasizing its use as a personal name rather than a common noun. This consistent use as a name connected to priestly or Levitical service reveals its rootedness in a heritage of work related to the Lord’s service.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַעֲשַׂי as 'work of the Lord' and as a name tied to priestly function invites reflection on the call to active service in God’s kingdom. The root meaning of 'to do' underscores the biblical emphasis on faith demonstrated through works, not merely belief alone. This reminds believers that their identity in Christ involves purposeful action aligned with God's will, just as the priest Maasiai represented faithful service after exile. It points to the continuity of God’s work through His people, who are called to carry out His purposes faithfully.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Chronicles 9:12 mentions 'Maasiai the son of Adiel,' situating him within a genealogical record of priestly descent. The use of מַעֲשַׂי here highlights a person whose name literally means 'work of the Lord,' emphasizing the importance of priestly labor in maintaining covenant faithfulness. This verse draws attention to the legacy of faithful service and the ongoing responsibility of God’s people to engage actively in His work.
